english.title: Knowingly as a trespasser live / intend to live in a residential building
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were in a residential building, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BUILDING..), and having entered it as a trespasser, lived or intended to live in the building
english.legislation: Contrary to section 144(1) and (5) of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment Act 2012.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and location

lived / intended to live in the building

english.notes:
(i) Section 144(2) of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment Act 2012 provides that is offence is not committed by a person holding over after the end of a lease or licence (even if the person leaves and re-enters the building).
(ii) Section 144(3) of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment Act 2012 provides that for the purpose of this section a"building" includes any structure or part of a structure (including a temporary or moveable structure), and a building is "residential" if it is designed or adapted, before the time of entry, for use as a place to live.
(iii) Section 144(4) of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment Act 2012 provides that for the purposes of this section the fact that a person derives title from a trespasser, or has the permission of a trespasser, does not prevent the person from being a trespasser.
(iv) Section 144(6) of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment Act 2012 provides that In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

other.penalty:
Summary: Fifty one weeks imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.. Note:
In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
